## 5.5 Carbon Prices Cut Emissions {#paper-5-5}

*Evidence from Ten Natural Experiments in Fuel Taxes, Carbon Pricing and Subsidy Reform*

Ministries weighing a carbon tax are usually shown a model's estimate of what it will do. This brief reports what happened instead, in ten cases where a carbon tax, a fuel tax, an emissions trading price, a subsidy cut or a price shock raised fuel prices and researchers later measured the effect. Every case shows a cut. In road transport and home heating, sustained prices cut emissions from the priced fuels by about 1 to 2 percent for each 10 dollars a tonne, building up over five to fifteen years. In power, where gas plants could replace coal, the cut per dollar was five to ten times larger. Taxes moved demand more than equal market price changes, while offsetting tax cuts, exemptions and unpriced coal weakened the effect. Ministries can plan on these magnitudes, and modelers should test their tools against these cases.
